preamble: The palatalization of the voiceless alveolar fricative [s] to the voiceless alveolo-palatal fricative [ɕ] before high front vowels and /j/. It occurs as allophony in Japanese, as a historical merger in Mandarin (the jiantuan merger of Middle Chinese *s- before front vowels), and in the inherited soft series of Polish.

examples.note: Original /si/ came to be pronounced [ɕi]; /s/ is realized as [ɕ] before /i/.
Loanword adaptation keeps the [ɕ] realization before /i/.
Middle Chinese *s- before high front vowels merged with palatalized velars as [ɕ].
Proto-Slavic *s before a front vowel became the soft sibilant ś [ɕ].

sources: Vance, T. J. (2008). The Sounds of Japanese. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521617543
Norman, J. (1988). Chinese. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521296533
